title: Outlook on Singapore’s Water Adequacy and Possibility of Water Rationing Exercises
what_it_is: Outlook on Singapore’s Water Adequacy and Possibility of Water Rationing Exercises

sections.label: Linggiu Reservoir and Singapore water supply
sections.summary: Linggiu Reservoir fell below 50% in September 2019, and Singapore has diversified water sources but no rationing since 1964.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: The water level at Linggiu Reservoir fell below 50% in September 2019, as the Public Utilities Board (PUB) had to discharge more water from the Linggiu Reservoir to supplement water flowing in the Johor River, in order to meet the total abstractions of both Malaysia and Singapore from the Johor River.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: If the Linggiu Reservoir fails, the Johor River may suffer low water levels, which will compromise Singapore's right to abstract our full entitlement of 250 million gallons of water per day under the 1962 Water Agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: So, if the Linggiu Reservoir water levels fall, Johor River may suffer low water levels.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We are following up with Malaysia on identifying appropriate and timely measures, including additional schemes, to increase the yield of the Johor River.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: In Singapore, Members may also recall photos on social media showing the falling water levels at the Botanic Gardens Eco Lake and Bedok Reservoir due to the dry spell.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: That said, there has not been a need for nationwide water rationing in Singapore since 1964.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Over the years, Singapore has developed a robust and diversified supply of water, as a result of our early and consistent investments in water infrastructure and research and development.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: We have augmented our water supply with weather-resilient sources, namely, NEWater and desalinated water.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: Along with water from local catchment and imported water, they make up Singapore's "Four National Taps".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: However, the production of NEWater and desalinated water is energy-intensive and costly.

sections.label: Climate change and dry spells
sections.summary: With climate change, Singapore has and will experience more extreme weather patterns, and prolonged dry spells will affect it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
sentences.text: With climate change, Singapore has and will experience more extreme weather patterns, and prolonged dry spells will affect us.
